channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 多少 / 几 · how many, how much
item.description: The two question words for quantity: 几 for small countable numbers and 多少 for larger or unknown amounts, why 几 needs a measure word and 多少 may skip it, and how to ask prices and ages.

item.title: 可能 · maybe, possible
item.description: The all-purpose word for possibility, working as adverb, adjective, and noun, and how it differs from 也许, 或许, 大概, and the modal 会.

item.title: 应该 · the modal "should"
item.description: The modal verb for "should, ought to," covering both moral obligation and confident inference, and how it differs from 得, 要, and 必须.

item.title: 一下 · the verb-softener
item.description: The verbal-quantity word that makes an action brief and casual, how verb + 一下 softens a request, and how it differs from verb reduplication and from the time-word 一会儿.

item.title: 帮助 · to help
item.description: The everyday word for help, both verb and noun, and how it differs from the lighter 帮 and the separable 帮忙 (to do a favor).

item.title: 工作 · work, job
item.description: The everyday word for work, both the activity and the job itself, and how it differs from 上班 (to go to work), 职业 (occupation), and 事业 (career).

item.title: 其实 · actually
item.description: The everyday adverb for "actually, in fact," used to correct an impression or reveal the real situation, and how it differs from 实际上, 事实上, and 本来.

item.title: 现在 · now
item.description: The everyday word for now, where it sits in a Chinese sentence, and how it differs from 目前 (at present), 此刻 (this very moment), and 如今 (nowadays).

item.title: 希望 · to hope
item.description: The everyday word for hope, both the verb and the noun, and how it differs from 想 (to want), 愿意 (to be willing), 盼望 (to long for), and 期待 (to look forward to).

item.title: 一会儿 · a short while
item.description: The everyday word for a little while, how it marks both a short duration and the near future, and how it differs from the verb-softener 一下 and from 等会儿.

item.title: 红楼梦 · Dream of the Red Chamber
item.description: The 18th-century novel that many call the greatest in the Chinese language: the slow decline of a great family, a doomed love among the young, and a sense that all the beauty and luxury of the world is a passing dream.

item.title: 三国演义 · Romance of the Three Kingdoms
item.description: The 14th-century novel that turned the wars after the Han into the great epic of Chinese loyalty and cunning. Sworn brothers, a god-like strategist, and the maxim that the realm long divided must unite.

item.title: 水浒传 · Water Margin
item.description: One hundred and eight outlaws, each driven from honest life by a corrupt officialdom, gather at the marsh of Liangshan to rob the rich and defy the state. The 14th-century novel of righteous banditry and brotherhood.

item.title: 西游记 · Journey to the West
item.description: A Buddhist monk, a rebellious immortal monkey, a glutton pig, and a river demon travel west for the scriptures. The 16th-century novel of pilgrimage, magic, and mischief that gave the world the Monkey King.

item.title: 给 · to give, for, and to
item.description: The verb "to give," the coverb that marks a recipient or beneficiary ("for/to"), and a colloquial passive marker, all from one character.

item.title: 还是 / 或者 · "or" in questions vs. statements
item.description: Chinese splits English "or" in two: 还是 offers a choice in a question, 或者 offers an alternative in a statement. Using the wrong one is a classic error.

item.title: 吗 · the yes-no question particle
item.description: The simplest way to ask a question in Mandarin: add 吗 to the end of a statement. Plus how it differs from A-not-A questions and from 呢 and 吧.

item.title: 一点儿 / 有点儿 · a little
item.description: The classic confusion pair: 有点儿 comes before an adjective and leans negative ("a bit too…"), while 一点儿 comes after and is neutral ("a little more").

item.title: 一样 / 像 · same and similar
item.description: How to say two things are the same (A 跟 B 一样) or alike (A 像 B), and how this differs from the unequal comparison with 比.

item.title: 在 · location, existence, and the progressive
item.description: One of the busiest words in Mandarin: the verb "to be at," the location coverb "at/in," and the progressive marker for ongoing action.

item.title: 兵马俑 · The Terracotta Army
item.description: Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, each with a different face, buried to guard the First Emperor in death. A farmer digging a well found them in 1974, and the silent army became the most astonishing archaeological discovery of the century.

item.title: 三国 · The Three Kingdoms
item.description: After the Han collapsed, China split into three rival states: Wei, Shu, and Wu. The sixty years of their wars produced the most beloved cast of heroes, traitors, and strategists in Chinese history.

item.title: 史记 · Records of the Grand Historian
item.description: Sima Qian wrote the founding work of Chinese historiography under the shadow of his own mutilation: a vast history from the legendary Yellow Emperor to his own Han dynasty, and the model every later dynastic history would follow.

item.title: 隋朝 · The Sui Dynasty
item.description: A short, ferocious dynasty that reunified China after nearly four centuries of division, dug the Grand Canal, and laid the institutions the glorious Tang would inherit, then burned itself out in a single generation.

item.title: 道德经 · Daodejing
item.description: Eighty-one short chapters of paradox and indirection that became the foundational text of Daoism and one of the most translated books in human history. The way that can be spoken is not the constant way.

item.title: 孙子兵法 · The Art of War
item.description: Thirteen terse chapters on conflict, attributed to the strategist Sun Wu, that became the oldest and most influential military treatise in the world. The supreme art is to subdue the enemy without fighting.

item.title: 觉得 · to think, to feel
item.description: The everyday verb for giving an opinion or impression, and how it differs from the more formal 认为 and from 想 (to want / to think over).

item.title: 朋友 · friend
item.description: The everyday word for friend, and the rich web of relationship terms (好朋友, 男朋友, 交朋友) built around it.

item.title: 时候 · time, moment
item.description: The everyday word for a point in time, and the indispensable 的时候 ("when") pattern that every learner needs.

item.title: 问题 · question, problem
item.description: One word for both "question" and "problem", and the everyday phrases (没问题, 有问题, 出问题) built from it.
